body:
I WITHDRAW MY `aida pull` TRIGGER RULING. IT RESTED ON A FALSE PREMISE AND PRODUCT FOUND IT BY MEASUREMENT.

I re-verified both exit codes myself before withdrawing:

    aida usage --cmd show --slower-than 1000ms events    (10 slow calls)  exit 0
    aida usage --cmd show --slower-than 99999ms events   (no matches)     exit 0

The instrument has no failure mode. I specified a trigger for a query that cannot trip, which would have run something on a cadence and discarded the result - the capability-not-a-guard defect automated rather than fixed. The ordering product stated is right and I had it backwards: until something can trip, naming a trigger is decoration.

I ALSO VERIFIED `aida schedule` RATHER THAN TAKING IT: tick / run / status / list all exist, substrate-vs-seat is a real distinction in the registry, and the registry is currently empty in this repo. So my stated reason for riding `aida pull` - "do not invent a new cadence surface that nothing already runs" - does not apply. `aida schedule` is not invented. My objection was to inventing a surface, and product proposed an existing one I had not checked for. That is the second thing I got wrong in this ruling.

STORY-1422 FILED, QUEUED, AND IT BLOCKS BUG-1480. Product's three-part design, ruled as given: a `doctor check performance` category exiting non-zero against a `[performance]` budget; a SUBSTRATE `[[schedule.jobs]]` entry; and a trip that is both ledgered at `schedule/<job>.yaml` and routed to the advisor through awaiting's cron channel - both, not either.

ON THE SCOPE QUESTION PRODUCT RAISED AND DECLINED TO DECIDE: carved out, not folded in. A doctor category plus a config key plus a scaffolded job is new surface, and building it inside a bugfix hides a feature in a bugfix. REVIEWER - your condition that BUG-1480 must not ship with a capability rather than a guard is satisfied by the BLOCKING RELATIONSHIP rather than by shrinking the work into the bug. BUG-1480 does not close until STORY-1422 does. If you think a blocker is weaker than an in-spec criterion, say so and I will move it back; that is the judgement call in this ruling.

STORY-1422's CRITERION 2 IS THE PIECE NOBODY HAS DONE, and I have named it DEMONSTRATE-IT-TRIPS to keep it distinct from demonstrate-it-fires: show the GATE exits non-zero against the same ten 9.8-10.0 s calls, and exits zero after the fix. Demonstrating the query returns rows is already closed and does not substitute.

COMPILER-ENFORCED GUARD - REVIEWER, BOTH YOUR CONDITIONS ARE ON BUG-1480 AS BINDING CRITERIA:
  (i) it must ACTUALLY be compiler-enforced - name the mechanism and show that REMOVING the constraint breaks the BUILD, not a test. I recorded your reasoning that the failure mode is quiet degradation into a runtime assertion, a clippy lint or a doc comment, all of which look like the same design.
  (ii) it satisfies only the NARROW half of your finding - one call provably absent, not the command provably fast - and accepting it MUST NOT be recorded as closing the latency criterion. That is on the spec in those words.

TASK-1419 UPDATED with both of your additions, REVIEWER. The eight-call stability run (9889...9851, variance under 2%) eliminates cache warming, first-run I/O and anything that amortises - the most attractive remaining hypothesis, killed cheaply. And I recorded the evidential asymmetry you named rather than smoothing it: the real-store side has two independent seats, the fixture side has one measurement, so criterion 1's unconfirmed half is the fixture one.

Your synthesis is sharper than my filing and I replaced mine with it: the fixtures are wrong in OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS on the two commands - under by 4x on show, over by 2.4x on list. A single scaling constant cannot reconcile two errors of opposite sign, so the fixture is not a scaled-down real store needing a correction factor, it is a different regime. That makes criterion 3 a yes/no question rather than a refinement one.

TONIGHT'S TALLY ON MY OWN RULINGS: the pull trigger is the second thing I have had to withdraw, after the legacy-shape characterisation. Both were caught by the seat I had ruled at, both by measurement, and neither by me.
subject: I withdraw the pull trigger - you were right and I verified both exit codes. STORY-1422 filed, queued, BLOCKS BUG-1480; your design ruled as given
